# Results — Study 929 (Rights Offering) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). A market-model event study
around **39 US rights offerings** by **20 listed issuers** (mostly closed-end funds, plus
two BDCs and a REIT), 2013–2023. Abnormal returns are measured against **SPY** with
alpha and beta estimated on the `(-250, -31)` trading-day window before each anchor.
Daily total-return closes (`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`), shared cache. As-of
**2026-06-30** (the partial current month is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 issuers + SPY (market) + BIL (cash) | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 | 5,406 | Fingerprint `9acc9535dfdd` |

Events listed **39**, usable **39**, dropped 0. Anchors run 2013-05 → 2023-09. The loaded
window is pinned at **both** ends (`data.START` as well as `data.AS_OF`): the shared
`studies/_cache` holds SPY back to 1993 for other studies, and an unpinned start would
change this study's fingerprint every time a neighbour extended a tape. (The fingerprint
still tracks the *content* of the shared parquet files: a neighbour re-fetching a ticker
re-stamps its adjusted closes, which is why this stamp is dated rather than eternal. Row
count, date range and every statistic below were unchanged by the last such re-stamp.)

**PROXY / ASSUMPTION inventory** — the three non-tape inputs, all swept below:

1. **The event list itself.** Hand-compiled from public rights-offering announcements;
   the anchor is accurate to the **month**, not the day. Every window is therefore ≥ 7
   trading days wide and the anchor is jittered ±10 calendar days.
2. **The rights timetable.** Per-deal record and expiry dates are not in the list, so
   ex-rights is modelled at anchor **+10** and expiry at anchor **+40** calendar days
   (the standard US schedule). Swept at 28 / 40 / 55 days.
3. **The discount band.** A coarse hand-assigned `deep` / `moderate` / `shallow` label,
   not a measured subscription price. Tested against a label permutation.

**The look-ahead this design cannot avoid, named.** Because the anchors are
month-precision, for roughly half the deals the anchor sits *before* the true press
release, so the calendar-time book is occasionally long a name whose news is not yet
public. That is a real look-ahead channel. Its direction matters: it can only manufacture
an announcement reaction a real-time trader would have missed, so it biases the study
**towards** finding an edge. The ±10-day anchor jitter sweeps it; nothing appears.

**Survivorship, named.** Five further deals we wanted (CUBA, NHF, ENZN, SPLP, TUEM) have
no retrievable Yahoo tape — delisted, merged or renamed. Rights offerings cluster in
distressed issuers, and distressed issuers are exactly the names that disappear, so the
retained sample is **survivor-biased towards the deals that ended well**. Any negative
result here is therefore, if anything, understated.

**Adjustment caveat.** `auto_adjust=True` neutralises splits and dividends but **not**
the rights issue: the theoretical ex-rights price drop stays in the tape as a raw fall,
even though a subscribing holder was compensated by the value of the right. The
*subscription* window therefore mixes news with **mechanical dilution**; the
*announcement* and *post-expiry* windows are clean, and the **signal** verdict is formed
on those. The same artefact reaches the tradable book — a `(+1, +49)` holding period
spans the modelled ex-rights date — so the book is reported over the full span **and**
over the ex-rights-free `(+29, +49)` span below.

## The three event windows (market-model CAR vs SPY, price-and-dividend total return)

| Window | trading days | n | mean CAR | median | cross-sec *t* | hit rate [Wilson] | bootstrap 95% |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Run-up | −20 … −2 | 39 | +1.08% | +0.55% | +1.20 | 54% [39%, 68%] | [−0.45%, +3.04%] |
| **Announcement** | −1 … +5 | 39 | **+0.27%** | −0.02% | **+0.34** | 49% [34%, 64%] | [−1.20%, +1.95%] |
| Subscription *(dilution mixed in)* | +1 … +28 | 39 | **−2.06%** | −1.13% | **−2.03** | 41% [27%, 57%] | [−4.07%, −0.05%] |
| **Post-expiry** | +29 … +49 | 39 | **+0.21%** | +0.44% | **+0.25** | 59% [43%, 73%] | [−1.51%, +1.87%] |

The cross-sectional *t* above is the naive one (39 deals treated as 39 independent
draws). It is not the number the verdict rests on; the placebos below are.

The announcement window is a **non-event**: +0.27%, *t* = +0.34, hit rate 49%, and the
bootstrap CI is symmetric about zero. The market neither punishes nor rewards the news
of a rights offering in these names.

## Is the deep discount compensated? No.

| Window | deep band (n=18) | moderate/shallow (n=21) | gap | Welch *t* | label-permutation *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Subscription | −2.74% | −1.47% | −1.27% | −0.60 | 0.530 |
| Post-expiry | −0.09% | +0.48% | −0.57% | −0.31 | 0.751 |

Deeper-discounted deals do **not** earn a compensating post-deal return; if anything they
run slightly worse, and a random relabelling of the bands reproduces that gap three times
out of four. The "gift" reading has no support in the cross-section.

## The one number that clears |*t*| = 2 — and why it does not survive

The subscription-window drift (−2.06%, *t* = −2.03) is the study's only nominally
significant result. It fails every check we can throw at it.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| **Placebo A — whole-tape anchors** (300 draws, 2005–2026) | placebo sd **2.03%** → *z* = **−0.93**, *p* = 0.21 |
| **Placebo B — era-matched anchors** (300 draws, 2012–2024) | placebo sd **1.28%** → *z* = **−1.60**, *p* = **0.09** |
| **Placebo C — clustered** (slide the whole list by one offset) | placebo sd **2.07%** → *z* = **−0.91**, *p* = 0.28 |
| **Leave-one-issuer-out** | *t* ranges −2.50 (drop SPE) to **−1.14** (drop CRF, one issuer's five deals) |
| **Era cut (2018)** | 2013–2017: −2.65% (*t* = −2.07) · 2018–2023: **−1.59% (*t* = −1.05)** |
| **Assumed timetable** | expiry 28d: −1.07% (*t* = −1.43) · 40d: −2.06% (−2.03) · 55d: −1.43% (−1.29) |
| **Anchor jitter ±10 calendar days** | *t* ∈ [−2.03, −1.57]; only the un-jittered anchor and +5d reach |*t*| = 2 at all |

**Which placebo to believe — and why we do not lean on it.** Placebo A draws pseudo-anchors
from the whole loaded tape, which hands it the 2008 and 2020 crashes: regimes in which
none of these deals was announced. That inflates its dispersion to 2.03% and makes the
observed drift look tame. **Placebo B is the fairer yardstick**: restrict the draws to the
years the deals actually happened and the dispersion falls to 1.28%, and the observed
drift becomes *z* = −1.60, *p* = 0.09 — still short of significance, but nothing like
"decisive". Placebo C keeps the calendar clustering of the real list intact (the two
Cornerstone funds every September, the Gabelli funds every April) and lands back near
A. So the honest statement is narrower than a single placebo makes it look: **the
subscription drift is not significant under the fair placebo, and it is not robust** —
one issuer, one era cut or one plausible timetable each take it below |*t*| = 1.5. And it
sits in the one window contaminated by mechanical ex-rights dilution, so even a real
drift there would be arithmetic, not news.

The announcement window flips sign with the jitter (+1.06% at −10 days, −0.69% at +5) —
the signature of noise.

## Tradability — the calendar-time portfolio (excess-of-cash, one execution lag)

Equal-weight book of every name currently inside its window, entered at the close of the
session **after** the announcement (the single lag), 25 bps one-way × NAV. Both legs are
excess-of-cash; the short leg is **credited its cash collateral** and pays borrow on top,
so the costs are not one-sided. The book is run twice: over the full `(+1, +49)` span,
which swallows the mechanical ex-rights drop (penalising the long leg, flattering the
short one), and over the ex-rights-free `(+29, +49)` span.

`alpha` is the beta-adjusted intercept against SPY excess-of-cash, HAC *t*. It is the
statistic to read: the long book is **long-only equity** 13–25% of the time, so its own
*t* mostly prices the equity risk premium it rents, and the vs-SPY Sharpe race is
exposure-mismatched in the other direction.

| Leg / span | excess Sharpe | own HAC *t* | alpha vs SPY | HAC *t*(α) | CAGR | max DD | vs SPY Sharpe adv. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Long, full `(+1,+49)` | +0.098 | +0.44 | **+0.03%/yr** | **+0.01** | +0.47% | −39.7% | −0.477 (*t* = −2.53) |
| Long, clean `(+29,+49)` | +0.448 | +2.03 | **+2.98%/yr** | **+1.79** | +3.17% | −22.1% | −0.127 (*t* = −2.05) |
| Short, full `(+1,+49)`, 300 bps borrow | −0.322 | −1.43 | −2.60%/yr | −1.02 | −4.28% | −73.6% | −0.897 (*t* = −3.05) |
| Short, clean `(+29,+49)`, 300 bps borrow | −0.730 | −3.24 | −5.12%/yr | −3.02 | −5.67% | −71.4% | −1.306 (*t* = −4.00) |
| SPY (excess-of-cash benchmark) | +0.575 | — | — | — | — | — | — |

Invested **25.3%** of sessions on the full span (averaging 1.4 names live) and **13.5%**
on the clean span (1.1 names) — a thin, concentrated book by construction.

Read the clean row carefully, because it is the strongest positive number in this study
and it is still not an edge: an excess Sharpe of +0.448 with an own *t* of +2.03 is what a
long-only equity sleeve earns for renting beta a seventh of the time. Price the beta out
and the alpha is **+2.98%/yr with a HAC *t* of +1.79** — under the bar, on a window that
was chosen *after* seeing that the full span was contaminated, and on the same 20 deeply
overlapping issuers whose event-study CAR over exactly that window is +0.21% (*t* =
+0.25). It also loses the Sharpe race to buying SPY.

**Cost sweep (long leg, full span, one-way × NAV):** gross Sharpe +0.168 → +0.140 (10 bps)
→ +0.098 (25 bps) → +0.028 (50 bps) → −0.110 (100 bps). There is nothing for costs to eat:
the gross edge is already inside the noise. **Borrow sweep (short leg, annualised, cash
collateral credited):** full span −0.256 (0 bps) → −0.278 (100) → −0.322 (300) → −0.431
(800); clean span −0.677 → −0.695 → −0.730 → −0.818. Negative at every rate on both
spans, so the "warning" trade is not salvageable by cheap borrow either.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports the stamp)

On a panel with a **planted** rights effect (announcement drop, subscription drift,
post-expiry bounce, 1.5× for the deep band) the harness recovers all three legs cleanly:
announcement −6.62% (*t* = −7.88), subscription −9.42% (*t* = −5.73), post-expiry +5.81%
(*t* = +4.96), and the deep-band split is found. On the **matched null** (same anchors,
effect switched off) the post-expiry window averages −0.19% across 12 seeds (sd 1.40) and
the announcement window +0.03% (sd 0.79). Across those 12 null seeds |*t*| ≥ 2 fires
**0** times on the post-expiry window, **0** on the announcement window and **1** on the
subscription window — about the rate chance dictates. That last one is worth dwelling on:
a single seed of pure noise can hand you a *t* of −2.05 on a 28-day window in this
universe, which is exactly the trap the real tape sets. The detector works and is
unbiased — the real-tape silence is a property of the deals, not of the harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** The announcement of a US rights offering moves these names by
  **+0.27% (*t* = +0.34)** against SPY, and the 20 sessions after the modelled expiry by
  **+0.21% (*t* = +0.25)**. Neither reading supports the folk claim that the deep
  subscription discount is compensated — and the cross-sectional split by discount depth
  finds nothing a coin toss would not (permutation *p* = 0.75). The single nominally
  significant number, the −2.06% subscription drift, sits in the one window contaminated
  by **mechanical, un-adjusted ex-rights dilution**; it does not clear the fair,
  era-matched placebo (*z* = −1.60, *p* = 0.09), and it collapses under a
  leave-one-issuer-out jackknife (*t* → −1.14), under the era cut (*t* → −1.05), under
  the assumed timetable (*t* → −1.29) and under the anchor jitter. Add a month-precision
  event list and a survivor-only sample and there is no robust |*t*| ≥ 2 anywhere in this
  study.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** The long "buy the discount" book earns an excess-of-cash
  Sharpe of **+0.098** over the full span with a beta-adjusted alpha of **+0.03%/yr**
  (HAC *t* +0.01). Strip the mechanical dilution out by holding only the clean
  post-expiry span and the book looks better — Sharpe +0.448 — but that is rented equity
  beta: alpha **+2.98%/yr, HAC *t* +1.79**, still under the bar, still behind SPY's
  +0.575, in a book of 1.1 illiquid closed-end funds live an eighth of the time through a
  −22% drawdown. The mirror-image short is negative at **every** borrow rate from 0 to
  800 bps on both spans. Neither direction is bankable; the discount is neither a gift
  nor a tradable warning, it is a distribution mechanic that leaves subscriber and
  non-subscriber roughly where the market already had them.
